newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks post fourth straight record close.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks post fourth straight record close.

text.p: CHANGE CHANGE

* Toronto 300 Index posted fourth record close this week * TSE helped by firmer Canada bonds, takeover action * 14 sub-groups evenly split * 85.9 million shares traded worth C$1.1 billion
Toronto's key 300 index hit its fourth straight record close on Thursday, but the overall market ended mixed as profit-takers offset gains due to firmer Canadian bonds and takeover action.
The TSE 300 Index climbed 4.24 points to 5276.30, surpassing the previous record close set on Wednesday.
The index also recorded a new intra-day high of 5278.75.

"Canada is outperforming the U.S. again. Our bond market looks stronger, but it's clear the markets are a bit nervous about inflation news," said Jim Doak, director of investment research for ScotiaMcleod Inc.
Declining stocks barely outnumbered advances 455 to 450, with 303 issues ending flat. Trading was brisk with volume of 85.9 million shares worth C$1.17 billion.
Toronto's 14 sub-groups finished even with banking, merchandising and communications leading the strong side.
Takeover target Loewen Group powered an 80-point rally in merchandising. But these gains were offset by profit-taking, particularly in transportation which sank 144 points.
Doak said the markets appear to be evenly divided on whether the U.S. Federal Reserve will raise interest rates.
--- HOT STOCKS ---
* Loewen Group Inc jumped 3.50 to 58 on 1.3 million shares amid market speculation that Service Corp's unsolicited bid for Loewen may succeed, but at a higher price.

* Laidlaw Inc class B topped the most-active list, falling 0.55 to 15 on 2.6 million shares. Some investors took profits after the stock soared on Wednesday on news of Laidlaw's sale of its solid waste unit. Analysts said the market may be concerned about what Laidlaw will do with the proceeds.
* Canadian banks were also very active. Royal Bank of Canada rose 0.20 to 38.10 on 1.2 million shares after earlier reaching a 52-week high of 38.25.
